lines.text: Look at the scar on its throat—that glowing iron! Someone harpooned this monster before us!
lines.journalNote: Isha saw a Tide Glow harpoon head lodged deep inside the Makara's armored gullet.

lines.text: Powder's dry. Guns are lashed. If the sea wants a fight, port broadside is ready to answer.
lines.journalNote: Gunner Isha stands vigilant by the port battery, smelling of sulfur and sea salt.

lines.text: Kedar's hounds are prowling. Let them try the guns—they'll get a rammer through the teeth.
lines.journalNote: Isha suspects the crew is turning, but she holds her battery against all comers.

lines.text: Thorne's dead in his cabin. Mutineers everywhere. But I won't abandon my cannons for a traitor's flag.
lines.journalNote: Isha refuses to swear loyalty to Kedar. She stays glued to the port broadside.

lines.text: Feel that vibration in the deck? It's coming from under the cargo grating. Not engine, not bilge. Something older.
lines.journalNote: Isha feels the Kaal Mani humming through the ship's timbers beneath the hold hatch.

lines.text: If we come about hard to port, I can bring all four cannons to bear on the monster. But someone has to hold the helm plate steady.
lines.journalNote: Isha needs the ship turned hard to port to expose the Makara's harpoon wound to her cannons.

lines.text: Navigator, give me clean firing lines. Steer us into the swell, not across it. I need this deck level when the beast surfaces.
lines.journalNote: Isha asked the Navigator to keep the ship level in the heavy swell.

lines.text: Quartermaster. I need dry powder kegs and slow matches, not another inventory lecture. Deliver the goods or man the guns yourself.
lines.journalNote: Isha demanded more powder kegs and slow matches from the Quartermaster.

lines.text: You! Haul that water tub closer to gun four. And if sparks fly, pour it on the cartridge, not your boots.
lines.journalNote: Isha ordered me to haul water tubs and keep fire off the powder deck.

lines.text: I spoke my piece. Clear the battery.
Gun captains don't repeat themselves, sailor. Move along.
Hover near my cannons again and I'll use your skull to ram the powder.
Four twelve-pounders, oiled and ready. But iron only bites what it can see.
I can smell the sulfur from the hold all the way up here on the gun deck.
Thorne gave the orders, but the sea doesn't care about rank or commissions.
The wind died an hour ago, yet the sails are straining. Something is pulling us.
Keep clear of the recoil ropes. If the monster hits the hull, these guns will dance.
I've fired into Spanish galleons and pirate sloops. Never fired at a mountain of black scale.
If you're going below, check the powder room vents. I don't want water in the barrels.
The sea's turned dark as pitch. Not even the moon leaves a reflection on this water.
My grandfather was a gunner out of Calicut. He told stories of the Makara—I thought they were fables.
Keep your head down if the firing starts. Grape shot doesn't care whose sash you wear.
A cannonball travels sixty fathom a second. The Makara moves faster.
Check the priming wire in your teeth. When steel strikes flint, don't blink.
